flow.title: Read the game
flow.body: Clock, holdings, available dealers and venue books form the current snapshot. The monitor archives the event stream and fills gaps from the feed.

flow.title: Choose a move
flow.body: Taker and maker policies rank trades and manage conversations. Duel policies negotiate their own price and delivery terms. Jev or the configured LLM supplies advisory verdicts.

flow.title: Pass the gates
flow.body: Validate the structured action against inventory, guardrails, approvals, breakers and the remaining tick window. The shared Postgres ledger coordinates accepts and listings.

flow.title: Send and record
flow.body: Python sends approved actions through the game client, backed by the vendored SDK. The organisers settle accepted trades on the next tick. Decisions and execution outcomes are recorded.

intelligence.title: Autonomous workers
intelligence.body: Trading and duel policies run on game ticks. A configurable Jev/LLM decider advises under a bounded budget; short ticks can fall back to Jev. Optional generated words do not replace structured prices.

intelligence.title: Interactive desk + MCP
intelligence.body: The Claude Agent SDK desk routes operator requests to strategist, buyer, seller and duelist roles. CLI and authenticated MCP tools use the same Python actions and guardrails; writes default to dry run.

intelligence.title: Feed learning + recall
intelligence.body: Feed and thread readers extract counterparty behaviour and outcomes. Optional LLM interpretation and local embeddings add context for future decisions; learning scopes keep duels and trading separate.

services.name: bazaar-taker
services.role: Buys from venue asks and negotiates dealer purchases. Public read-only /health, /state and WebSocket /events.

services.name: bazaar-maker
services.role: Posts and maintains asks/bids; runs the venue broker. An optional dealer-sell desk can negotiate sales when enabled. Public read-only status and events.

services.name: bazaar-duels
services.role: Negotiates scheduled duels and coordinates the shared accept slot with trading workers. Duel scoring is separate from card trading.

services.name: bazaar-mcp
services.role: Team tools over authenticated Streamable HTTP at /mcp. Human approval tools require a separate approver credential. /health is public.

services.name: bazaar-sim
services.role: Standalone simulated game API with synthetic team keys and an isolated bazaar_sim database. Real workers are not configured to target it.

services.name: phoenix
services.role: OpenTelemetry trace collection and a login-protected inspection UI. Persistent storage is separate from the trading database.

services.name: bazaar-live
services.role: Separate presentation repository: agent views, voice narration and operator screens. Server-side credentials protect game views and approval flows.

storage.title: Operational state
storage.body: Postgres stores holdings, feed history, traders, decisions, executions, approvals and the action ledger. The CLI monitor uses SSE plus feed polling; agents also read the market through their runtime.

storage.title: Memory for decisions
storage.body: Learnings retain their evidence and scope. Retrieval can combine text search with local fastembed vectors when pgvector is available. The simulator keeps its world in a separate database.

storage.title: Logs + observability
storage.body: Decisions and executions are inspectable records, with local JSONL fallbacks for supported logs. Per-service volumes hold local state and PAUSE files; Phoenix receives traces. A local log does not replace shared write coordination.

boundaries.title: Money and inventory
boundaries.body: GUARDRAILS.md is the checked-in policy source for holdings protection, price limits and approval thresholds. Actions recheck inventory and refuse moves that fail their gates; model verdicts cannot grant an override.

boundaries.title: One team budget
boundaries.body: Every process shares the game key and its request limits. Game ticks set deadlines; the ledger coordinates action quotas across machines. Local PAUSE files stop writes for the processes using that data directory.

boundaries.title: Public vs privileged
boundaries.body: Agent status endpoints expose a redacted view. Runtime tools require authentication, approvals have a separate privilege, and counterparty messages remain untrusted data. Live mode is an operator-controlled setting.

development.title: Python + Postgres
development.body: Python 3.12, uv, Pydantic, Typer and psycopg form the application stack. Docker Compose supplies local Postgres with pgvector and Phoenix. The presentation UI lives in bazaar-live.

development.title: Focused CI
development.body: Depot runs the linter, formatter, unit tests and Postgres integration tests. Simulator scenarios and evaluation tools are available for targeted experiments outside the required CI checks.

development.title: Reproducible docs
development.body: The README status and this page have deterministic generators. Architectural facts live here; task history and implementation plans remain in the local backlog rather than a stale deployment timeline.
